title: Your pencils
say: Four pencils today, chosen by value: two-H and H-B for your brightest areas, two-B for the mid-tones, and six-B for your very darkest darks. We'll use all four, one at a time.

title: A tissue for blending
say: You'll also reach for a small tissue later on, to blend your shading smooth. We'll get there in a few steps — for now, just know it's coming.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip — that's what gives foil its soft, believable shine.

title: Where your balloon will sit
say: Before the first line — leave space around your balloon. It sits slightly off-centre, a little tilted, so check the size before any detail. Lightly mark where your balloon will sit. I'll wait.

title: Find the tilt before the outline
watchSay: Watch for the tilt — the teacher's first lines aren't straight up and down. They lean, just slightly, crossing near the middle.
say: Now your turn — lightly cross two tilted guide lines near your centre mark. Take your time. I'll wait.

card.title: Find the tilt before the outline
card.sub: Compare the guide lines before adding detail.

title: Block in the whole shape first
watchSay: Keep going all the way around — block in the whole star before fixing any single point. Size first, detail later.
say: Rough in all six points lightly, all the way around. Don't worry about perfect symmetry yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Block in the whole shape first
card.sub: Size and placement matter before any detail.

title: Turn corners into soft curves
watchSay: Watch the teacher keep adjusting the edges — drawing, checking, and redrawing until the shape feels right. Even teachers correct their lines. That's how a good shape is found.
say: Your turn. Soften each corner into a gentle curve. If a line looks wrong, just adjust it — the teacher does too. I'll wait.

card.title: Turn corners into soft curves
card.sub: Foil has volume: let the edges bend.

title: Clean up with a light touch
watchSay: The teacher keeps refining this pass — a light touch, going back over a line that still needs adjusting before it's final.
say: Keep refining your own lines too, with a light touch. Nothing needs to be perfect yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Clean up with a light touch
card.sub: A light touch while the shape still settles.

title: Erasing the guide lines
watchSay: Now the teacher erases the guide lines. They helped us find the tilt and the shape at the start. The outline is set now, so we don't need them anymore.
say: Gently erase your guide lines too, and keep your outline. Take your time.

card.title: Erasing the guide lines
card.sub: The tilt lines did their job — now let them go.

title: Separate the seam from the outline
watchSay: Look closely at the rim just inside the outline — that seam is separate from the outer edge, and it matters.
say: Add a thin line just inside your outline, like a seam. Keep that narrow gap visible. I'll wait.

card.title: Separate the seam from the outline
card.sub: Look for the narrow rim inside the edge.

title: Let folds turn toward the centre
watchSay: These small curves are folds in the foil. Notice how they turn from the rim toward the centre, not straight across.
say: Add a few light fold lines, curving in toward the middle. Just a few is enough. I'll wait.

card.title: Let folds turn toward the centre

title: Your outline is ready
watchSay: A few more fold marks, and the outline is complete — a strong shape with soft edges, ready for shading.
say: Take one more look at your whole outline before we bring in the light and dark. I'll wait.

title: Outline complete
hint: Your outline is ready — next time, we bring in the light and dark.
say: Your outline is ready. That's the hardest part done — next time, we bring in the light and dark.
